Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, VP of Exploration; Robert Kline, VP of Marketing; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Michael Torres, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust EBITDA growth of 32% year-over-year, highlighting the strength of our asset base and operational discipline. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on production volumes, which rose 11.2% year-over-year to 278,500 BOE per day, with oil volumes hitting a record high. We are focused on capital efficiency, coming in under budget on key expenditures while advancing high-return drilling programs. Further, we are working on reserve additions that delivered a 185% replacement ratio, fueled by organic growth across our key basins. We continue to adjust to market dynamics through smart hedging that protected realizations and captured upside. We are advancing our midstream infrastructure to support growing throughput volumes. We are evaluating exploration opportunities like our Suriname appraisal successes. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance sustainability, with incident rates down significantly.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.15 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $620 million, and net income was $465 million. We generated $725 million in free cash flow and returned $500 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $3.2 billion in debt and $1.6 billion in cash.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—thank you for joining us on Apex Energy's third quarter earnings call. I'll dive right into our EBITDA performance, which came in at $825 million for the quarter, marking a robust 32% year-over-year increase from $625 million in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, our adjusted EBITDA now stands at $3.2 billion, up 28% from $2.5 billion a year ago. This outperformance underscores the strength of our asset base, operational discipline, and proactive capital allocation in a volatile macro environment.

First and foremost, realized pricing was a major tailwind. Our realized crude oil price averaged $82 per barrel in Q3, up 15% from $71 per barrel last year, driven by Brent crude sustaining above $85 per barrel amid OPEC+ production cuts and resilient global demand. Natural gas realizations held steady at $3.25 per MMBtu, benefiting from Henry Hub prices averaging $2.90—about 20% higher year-over-year—thanks to strong LNG export demand from Europe and Asia. NGLs contributed nicely too, at $28 per barrel, supported by Mont Belvieu fractionation spreads widening to $18 per barrel amid petrochemical pull-through. Overall, this pricing dynamic added approximately $140 million to our quarterly EBITDA, or about 45% of the total year-over-year growth.

Production volumes grew 12% year-over-year to 285,000 BOE per day, with oil comprising 68% of the mix. In the Permian Basin—our core growth engine—output hit a record 180,000 BOE per day, up 18% year-over-year, fueled by the completion of our Dagger Draw development program. We brought online 45 new horizontal wells in the Delaware sub-basin, averaging 1,200 lateral feet with our enhanced 'Super Frac' design: 50-stage completions using 4,000 pounds per foot proppant and 30 bpm slurry rates. This drove initial production rates north of 2,000 BOE per day per well, with 60-day initial productions 25% above type curve. Eagle Ford added another 8% volume growth to 65,000 BOE per day, leveraging our condensate-rich Karnes Trough acreage amid favorable Waha Hub differentials narrowing to -$0.15 per MMBtu.

Regionally, the U.S. onshore assets were the star performers, accounting for 92% of production and delivering 85% of the volume-driven EBITDA lift. Offshore Gulf of Mexico faced headwinds from Hurricane Francine disruptions, idling our Lobster Field FPSO for 12 days and curbing output by 5,000 BOE per day. However, we mitigated this through rapid restarts and insurance recoveries, limiting the EBITDA impact to just $15 million. Internationally, our Suriname Block 58 offshore partnership with TotalEnergies progressed with the Roystone-3 appraisal well spudding ahead of schedule, de-risking 500 million barrels of oil equivalent contingent resources—but no material production contribution yet.

On the cost side, we continue to extract efficiencies across the board. Lease operating expenses dropped 8% year-over-year to $8.50 per BOE, thanks to our digital oilfield initiatives: deploying IoT sensors and AI-driven predictive maintenance across 70% of our Permian pads, which reduced unplanned downtime by 22%. Gathering and transportation costs held flat at $4.20 per BOE despite higher volumes, aided by long-haul crude commitments to Gulf Coast refiners at attractive tariffs. Capex efficiency improved markedly, with DD&A per BOE at $12.40—down 5%—reflecting our shift to longer laterals and simultaneous frac crews, dropping drilling times to 18 days from spud-to-rig-release in the Permian.

Hedging played a smart hedge against volatility. With 65% of our oil volumes hedged via collars at $75-$90 per barrel and 45% of gas via swaps at $2.80 floor, we captured upside while protecting $120 million in realized gains during the quarter's WTI contango periods. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. I'll now turn to our operational performance, starting with production volumes, which remain the cornerstone of our value creation in this volatile macro environment. As you know, we're focused on high-return inventory in the core of the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford, leveraging our proprietary multi-well pad development strategy to drive capital efficiency.

For Q3 2024, we averaged 278,500 BOE per day total production, marking a solid +2.3% increase quarter-over-quarter from 272,100 BOE per day in Q2 and a robust +11.2% year-over-year from 250,400 BOE per day in Q3 2023. This outperformance reflects the successful ramp-up of our seven-well Vega pad in the Delaware Basin and four-well Dorado pad in the Eagle Ford, both brought online mid-quarter with initial production rates exceeding 2,500 BOE per day per well—about 15% above our type curve thanks to optimized slickwater fracs with 4,500 pounds per foot proppant and 40 bpm rates.

Oil production hit a record 172,000 barrels per day, up +3.1% quarter-over-quarter from 166,900 barrels per day in Q2 and +14.7% year-over-year from 149,900 barrels per day last year. The oil cut improved to 62% of total volumes, our highest in five quarters, driven primarily by Permian contributions which accounted for 68% of our oil output. In the Delaware, we drilled 18 gross operated wells with lateral lengths averaging 11,500 feet—up from 10,000 feet a year ago—yielding 30-day initial productions of 1,800 barrels per day oil per well. Eagle Ford oil volumes grew 8% quarter-over-quarter to 42,000 barrels per day, benefiting from our ESP artificial lift conversions, which have boosted runtime to 98% from 92% year-over-year.

Natural gas production, on an equivalent basis, averaged 106,500 BOE per day (or 639 million cubic feet per day gross), which was flat quarter-over-quarter from 106,200 BOE per day in Q2 but up +3.8% year-over-year from 102,600 BOE per day. The sequential stability masks some strong underlying trends offset by planned downtime. Haynesville gas, which makes up 55% of our NGL-rich gas mix, delivered +5% year-over-year growth to 350 million cubic feet per day, supported by two new 3-mile laterals with our high-intensity fracs using 100-mesh sand for enhanced fracture complexity. We curtailed about 15 million cubic feet per day in Q3 due to soft Henry Hub pricing averaging $2.85 per MMBtu—below our $3.00 economic threshold—but this was more than offset by premium realizations from our Cheniere LNG-linked contracts at $4.20 per MMBtu DES.

Regionally, the Permian drove 72% of our total growth, with Delaware volumes up 16% year-over-year to 145,000 BOE per day amid favorable WTI pricing around $82 per barrel strip. Eagle Ford contributed 22% of volumes at 58,000 BOE per day, flat quarter-over-quarter but resilient despite Texas weather disruptions that idled rigs for three days. Our Bakken pilot—two extended laterals in the TFX—added 4,500 BOE per day incrementally, with breakevens now at $55 per barrel thanks to our in-house ceramic diverters reducing water cuts by 12%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q2 earnings call for Apex Energy Corp. I'll now dive into our realized pricing dynamics for oil and natural gas, with a particular focus on the meaningful impact of our disciplined hedging programs. As you know, in a market characterized by heightened volatility—driven by persistent OPEC+ production cuts, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, and softening global demand signals from China—our hedging strategy has been a cornerstone of value protection and cash flow predictability.

In Q2, our realized oil price averaged $76.45 per barrel, a solid 8% sequential improvement from Q1's $70.82 per barrel and up 12% year-over-year. This compares favorably to the NYMEX WTI prompt month average of $81.25 per barrel during the quarter. On the gas side, we realized $3.12 per MCF, which was 5% higher than Q1's $2.97 per MCF but flat year-over-year, against a Henry Hub benchmark averaging $3.45 per MCF. These realized prices reflect not just basin-level differentials but, crucially, the protective overlay from our hedging portfolio, which covered approximately 62% of our Q2 oil production and 55% of gas volumes.

Our oil realizations benefited from a $2.15 per barrel uplift directly attributable to hedging. Without hedges, our realized price would have been around $74.30 per barrel, pressured by Permian Basin differentials averaging -$1.75 per barrel to WTI—wider than our historical norm of -$1.20 per barrel due to ongoing midstream constraints at Waha Hub and increased flaring restrictions under Texas Railroad Commission rules. Specifically, we had swaps in place for 40% of volumes at a weighted average floor of $72.50 per barrel, collars covering 15% with an average floor of $70 per barrel and ceiling of $85 per barrel, and three-way collars on 7% providing additional upside participation above $90 per barrel. These instruments, transacted with counterparties like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, locked in gains during WTI's intra-quarter rally from $78 to $84 per barrel in late June, while shielding us from the early-quarter dip below $77 amid inventory builds reported by the EIA.

For natural gas, the hedging impact was even more pronounced, adding $0.42 per MCF to our realizations. Absent hedges, we'd have seen $2.70 per MCF, as Haynesville differentials averaged -$0.35 per MCF to Henry Hub—reflecting robust regional production growth outpacing takeaway capacity on pipelines like GTN and Tennessee Gas. Our program included fixed-price swaps on 35% of volumes at $3.00 per MCF, puts on 15% at a $2.80 per MCF strike, and basis swaps that narrowed our exposure to Waha-like volatility in the Haynesville, where spot prices briefly touched $2.20 per MMBtu. This structure allowed us to capture 92% of Henry Hub upside during the quarter's mid-month spike to $3.70 per MCF, driven by LNG export ramps at Sabine Pass and Freeport.

Strategically, our hedging approach remains opportunistic and asymmetric, targeting 50-70% coverage on the next 12-24 months to balance downside protection with commodity upside. Looking forward, we now have 68% of Q3 oil production hedged at $74.20 per barrel, 52% for Q4 at $73.80 per barrel, and up to 45% for 2025 at $72.50 per barrel—all while maintaining a portfolio duration under 18 months to avoid over-hedging into a potential supply response from non-OPEC producers like those in the Permian and Guyana. On gas, we've layered in additional Winter 24/25 collars at $2.90-$4.20 per MMBtu for 40% coverage, anticipating Winter demand from data center electrification and European LNG displacement.

Regionally, our Eagle Ford assets realized $77.20 per barrel—bolstered by proximity to Corpus Christi refiners—while Permian barrels faced headwinds from local crude rejections at Cushing, averaging $75.10 per barrel post-hedge. In Appalachia, our modest Utica gas position fetched $2.85 per MCF realized, enhanced by firm transport on the Mountain Valley Pipeline, which came online ahead of schedule.

In summary, our hedging programs delivered over $145 million in incremental cash flow in Q2 alone, equivalent to 15% of our adjusted EBITDA, underscoring the value of our risk management framework amid Brent's 10% volatility and WTI's realized backwardation. This discipline positions us exceptionally well as we navigate macro uncertainties, including potential Fed rate cuts and the IEA's downward revisions to 2024 demand growth.

Now, turning to our capital expenditure performance, where we continue to demonstrate the operational discipline that's central to our returns-focused strategy in this $75 to $85 WTI environment. For the first half of 2024, our total upstream Capex came in at $1.05 billion, under our full-year guidance midpoint of $2.1 billion and 8% below our H1 budget of $1.14 billion. This variance reflects a combination of strong execution efficiencies, selective deferrals on non-core facilities, and proactive supply chain management amid lingering inflation in proppant and steel.

Drilling Capex: Budget $390 million versus actual $365 million, a -6.4% underrun. Drilling represented 35% of our H1 upstream budget but only 34.7% of actual spend, underscoring our relentless focus on cost per foot reductions and cycle time compression. We achieved this through our rollout of Schlumberger's DrillOps on Demand digital platform across our Permian fleet, which integrated real-time AI-driven pore pressure prediction and geomechanics modeling, shaving an average of 0.8 days off spud-to-TD times. In the Permian Basin, 65% of drilling activity, budget $255 million actual $235 million (-7.8%). Here, our seven-rig program averaged $1,450 per lateral foot—down 12% year-over-year—thanks to optimized rotary steerable systems from Halliburton and extended lateral lengths averaging 11,500 feet in the Delaware sub-basin. Bakken budget $85 million actual $82 million (-3.5%). Eagle Ford budget $50 million actual $48 million (-4%). Overall, drilling cost per foot fell 10% year-over-year to $1,380, with rig release rates holding steady at 22 days per well.

Completions Capex: Budget $480 million versus actual $505 million (+5.2%). Completions, at 43% of budget, came in slightly over due to targeted inflation offsets in sand and hydraulic horsepower, partially mitigated by our shift to slickwater fracs and cube development strategies. Actual spend hit 48.1% of total Capex, reflecting higher activity to support our 65-well H1 program versus 58 planned. Proppant costs rose 8% quarter-over-quarter on Northern White Sand constraints, but we locked in 70% of our 2024 sand requirements at $45 per ton via multi-year contracts with Hi-Crush. We executed 15 cube frac pads in the Permian—up from 10 in H1 2023—using simultaneous fracturing across 48 wells, which boosted our frac efficiency to 450 stages per day per fleet, a 25% improvement via Liberty Energy's OneStim integrated service. Permian 70% budget $340 million actual $360 million (+5.9%). Bakken budget $90 million actual $92 million (+2.2%). Eagle Ford budget $50 million actual $53 million (+6%).

Facilities Capex: Budget $270 million versus actual $180 million (-33.3%). Facilities, budgeted at 24% of total, dropped to 17.2% of actuals as we deferred $90 million in non-FID compression and water management projects. This strategic pull-forward aligns with our midstream joint ventures, including our 40% stake in the Matterhorn Express Pipeline JV with Kinder Morgan. Permian water infrastructure: deferred $40 million on produced water recycling plants. Bakken gathering systems: $25 million actual versus $40 million budget. Eagle Ford electrification: $15 million spent on converting two pads to electric frac fleets.

In summary, our H1 Capex underrun of 8% generated $200 million in free cash flow at current strips, exceeding expectations and supporting our progressive dividend and $500 million buyback authorization. Looking forward, Q3 activity ramps to 75 gross wells, with Capex cadence weighted to H2 at 55/45.

Strategically, this EBITDA growth positions us well for sustained free cash flow generation. We've returned 60% of FCF to shareholders via $400 million in buybacks and a 15% dividend hike, while allocating 25% to high-return Permian inventory—now over 5 years at current pace. Looking ahead, we guide Q4 EBITDA at $850-$900 million, assuming WTI $80-$85 and Henry Hub $2.75-$3.25.

I will now turn the call over to David Chen for an operational update.

David Chen: Thank you, Maria. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 278,500 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Dagger Draw pads online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, as Maria detailed with LOE down to $8.50 per BOE and drilling efficiencies.

These results underscore our disciplined approach: we're on track for full-year guidance of 275,000-285,000 BOE per day, with 60% oil mix, funded by $1.2 billion capex skewed 65% to Permian completions. We've deferred two gas-rich Haynesville pads to Q4 amid oversupply pressures from LNG export ramp-ups at Golden Pass and Plaquemines, prioritizing FCF over volume. Looking ahead, our 2025 plan calls for 5-7% total growth, anchored by 50 new Permian wells with child-parent optimization informed by our fiber-optic DAS/DTS data analytics, targeting 10% next-twelve-months uplift in EURs. This positions us well against peers like Pioneer and EOG, where we're trading at a 15% discount to PV-10 despite superior DD&A efficiency at $8.50 per BOE.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware and are planning to drill 20 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio. Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. This is Lisa Patel, VP of Exploration at Apex Energy Corporation. I'm pleased to dive into one of our strongest performance metrics this quarter: our proved reserves additions, with a particular focus on reserve replacement ratio and organic growth. As you know, in the Oil & Gas sector, maintaining a robust reserves book is the lifeblood of long-term value creation, especially in a volatile commodity environment where WTI has hovered around $75-80 per barrel and Brent at $78-82 amid ongoing OPEC+ production discipline.

For the full year 2023, we added 1.45 billion barrels of oil equivalent—or MMboe—to our proved reserves base, a robust 18% increase year-over-year from 1.23 billion MMboe in 2022. This brings our total year-end proved reserves to 5.2 billion MMboe, up 12% sequentially. These additions were achieved at a finding and development—or F&D—cost of just $12.50 per boe, well below our five-year average of $14.20 and competitive with peers like Pioneer Natural Resources at $11-13 and EOG Resources around $13-15. This efficiency underscores our disciplined capital allocation in a high-return inventory.

Our total RRR for 2023 clocked in at 185%, meaning we replaced 1.85 barrels for every barrel produced. To put that in context, our 2023 production averaged 785,000 boe per day—or roughly 286 million MMboe annually—across our diversified portfolio. That's a substantial improvement from 162% in 2022 and well above our three-year average of 155%. Our organic RRR—excluding any acquisitions—was an even stronger 172%, highlighting the quality of our internal engine.

Organic reserves grew by 1.33 billion MMboe, driven primarily by positive revisions and extensions & discoveries. Revisions contributed 620 million MMboe, or 43% of the total, largely from better-than-expected well performance and reservoir performance in our core shale plays. Extensions and discoveries added 710 million MMboe, fueled by successful appraisal drilling.

In the Permian Basin, our flagship asset, we added 580 million MMboe, representing 40% of organic additions. Here, longer laterals—averaging 12,500 feet in the Delaware sub-basin—and enhanced completions with 4,500 pounds of proppant per foot drove PDP-to-PUD conversions. Our Northern Midland acreage saw a 25% reserve uplift from second-vintage Wolfcamp A wells outperforming type curves by 15% EUR—estimated ultimate recovery. This positions us with over 3,000 drilling locations at sub-$40 WTI breakevens.

Shifting to the Eagle Ford, we booked 290 million MMboe in additions, up 22% year-over-year, from infill development in our Karnes County window. Optimized frac designs, incorporating dissolvable diverters and high-conductivity ceramics, boosted initial production rates by 18% to over 1,800 boe per day per well, with 20% lower F&D costs at $10.80 per boe.

Offshore Gulf of Mexico contributed 220 million MMboe, or 15% of organic growth, highlighted by our Lucius South appraisal success in Green Canyon Block 875. High-resolution 4D seismic, integrated with machine learning reservoir models, de-risked a 150-million-MMboe PUD extension at under $25 per boe F&D.

Internationally, we added 240 million MMboe, primarily from our Suriname Block 58 offshore campaign—modeled after ExxonMobil's neighboring Stabroek block in Guyana. The Roystone-2 appraisal well encountered 120 feet of net high-quality oil pay in the Campanian interval, certifying 180 million MMboe proved.

These organic additions reflect our "high-grading" philosophy: focusing on low-decline, high-IPR inventory. We've invested heavily in technical initiatives like full-waveform inversion seismic for better subsalt imaging in GoM and AI-driven sweet-spot mapping in shale, which improved success rates from 85% to 92% in new wells. Looking ahead, with an RRR north of 160% targeted for 2024-2026, we see 15-20% annual reserve expansion without M&A dilution.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Robert Kline to discuss our marketing strategy.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our NGL-rich production in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of our midstream assets is significant. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. I'd like to dive into our Midstream segment, which continues to deliver robust results amid strong upstream production growth and resilient demand dynamics. As you know, our midstream portfolio is anchored by a diversified suite of fee-based assets, including over 10,000 miles of crude oil and natural gas pipelines, 50 million barrels of crude storage capacity, and strategic fractionation and rail loading facilities across key U.S. basins. In Q3, the segment generated $450 million in adjusted EBITDA, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, driven primarily by higher transportation volumes and the ramp-up of recently completed infrastructure projects. Tariff revenues hit a record $1.2 billion for the quarter, supported by 92% utilization across our crude pipeline network—well above our long-term average of 85%—and an average realized tariff of $1.45 per barrel-mile on crude, up 8% from last year due to contractual escalators and spot market strength.

Total system throughput averaged 3.2 million barrels per day for crude oil equivalents, a 14% increase year-over-year and 7% above Q2 levels. Crude volumes reached 2.1 million barrels per day, up 16% year-over-year, fueled by Permian Basin production surging past 6.5 million barrels per day basin-wide. Our Longhorn Pipeline, which we expanded to 850,000 barrels per day capacity last year in JV with DCP Midstream, operated at 95% utilization, transporting WTI-priced Permian crude directly to Nederland, Texas. Natural gas liquids volumes hit 750,000 barrels per day, +12% year-over-year, benefiting from Haynesville fractionation demand; our Mont Belvieu complex processed 420,000 barrels per day. On the dry gas side, we transported 4.8 Bcf per day, up 11% year-over-year, with Appalachia volumes leading at 2.2 Bcf per day via our Mountain Valley Pipeline stake.

The Permian remains our growth engine, accounting for 55% of volumes. Eagle Ford contributed 15% of volumes, with steady 400,000 barrels per day from our Corpus Christi laterals. We're executing on a disciplined $2.5 billion capex program for 2024, with key milestones including mechanical completion of the 42-inch, 350-mile Apex Permian Connector pipeline from Waha to the El Paso gateway, now commissioning at 800,000 barrels per day initial capacity—expandable to 1.2 million barrels per day. We've also progressed our Bakken Gas Processing Plant #3 to 75% complete, a 200 million cubic feet per day facility.

Technically, we're leaning into digital initiatives: Our AI-driven predictive analytics platform, deployed across 80% of pipelines, has reduced downtime by 22%. On the sustainability front, we've electrified 40% of Permian pump stations with renewables, cutting Scope 1 emissions by 15% year-over-year. Looking forward, Q4 volumes guidance is 3.3-3.5 million barrels per day equivalents, with midstream EBITDA of $460-480 million.

I will now turn it over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Robert. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity. Thank you, and now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, our Chief Sustainability Officer—or HSSE—for an update on our environmental performance, including spills, incidents, and remediation efforts.

I'm pleased to report that fiscal 2023 marked another year of strong environmental stewardship at Apex Energy, with our total recordable environmental incidents down 28% year-over-year to just 14 events, the lowest in our five-year history. This performance not only exceeds our internal targets but also benchmarks favorably against peers—our spill volume of 1,247 barrels of hydrocarbons released is 35% below the American Petroleum Institute's upstream average of 1,920 barrels per operator of our scale.

Of those 14 incidents, 9 were minor non-hydrocarbon releases—primarily produced water from our onshore pads in the Permian Basin, totaling under 500 barrels. Crude oil spills accounted for 4 events, with a combined volume of 742 barrels, and one pipeline rupture in our Midstream segment released 5 barrels of dilbit. Notably, we had zero Tier 1 spills—those exceeding 1,000 barrels or with significant ecological impact—as defined by the EPA and BSEE.

Trend-wise, we've seen a consistent 15-20% annual decline in spill frequency since 2020, driven by our $250 million investment in digital twins and AI-powered predictive analytics across our 12,000-mile pipeline network and 5,500 active wells. In the Permian, where we operate over 2,500 pads, spill rates dropped to 0.12 incidents per 1,000 wells—half the EIA-reported basin average—thanks to real-time fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing on 85% of our laterals, which flagged 47 potential leaks before they escalated.

In the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, we recorded 3 incidents totaling 312 barrels, all contained within secondary containment on platforms. Onshore U.S., Permian and Eagle Ford dominated with 8 incidents, but remediation was swift—average first-response time of 18 minutes via our drone-equipped rapid-response teams. Internationally, our North Sea assets saw zero spills, and in Brazil's pre-salt Santos Basin, one minor 15-barrel produced water release was fully remediated within 72 hours.

Turning to remediation efforts—our "Respond, Restore, Reclaim" framework ensured 100% of 2023 spills were fully mitigated, with over 98% of impacted soils and waters returned to pre-incident baselines per EPA Method 1664 testing. Total remediation costs came in at $18.4 million, representing just 0.2% of our opex. Key highlights include rapid containment with 1,200 absorbent booms and 450 spill-skimmers, achieving 95% recovery rates. For Permian soil impacts, we applied microbial consortia, accelerating hydrocarbon degradation by 60%. Post-remediation, we utilized LiDAR-equipped drones and hyperspectral imaging to verify no residual plumes.

Lower incident rates have cut unplanned downtime by 22% to 1.2% of production—equating to $45 million in preserved EBITDA—and reduced our environmental insurance premiums by 15%. Looking ahead, we're accelerating our Zero Routine Flaring and Zero Spill ambitions, with $150 million allocated in 2024 for cathodic protection retrofits and machine learning leak detection via our partnership with Palantir.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Torres to discuss our technology initiatives.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. We are leveraging technology to improve our operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to optimize our operations. We are also exploring new technologies such as carbon capture and storage. Our digital oilfield initiatives include IoT sensors and AI-driven predictive maintenance across 70% of Permian pads, reducing downtime by 22%. We've rolled out Schlumberger's DrillOps and fiber-optic DAS/DTS for frac optimization, alongside AI for reservoir modeling and leak detection.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Walsh with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on EBITDA YoY change and key drivers?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, Brian. As Maria covered extensively, our $825 million EBITDA reflected a 32% year-over-year increase driven by higher realized prices—oil at $82 per barrel, gas at $3.25 per MMBtu—adding $140 million, plus 12% production growth to 285,000 BOE per day led by Permian. Cost efficiencies like 8% lower LOE to $8.50 per BOE and hedging gains of $120 million rounded it out, positioning us for Q4 guidance of $850-900 million.

Operator: Our next question comes from Elena Torres with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Elena Torres: Good morning. What are your expectations for production volumes next quarter and full year, including factors influencing projections?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Elena. Happy to dive into that. We're guiding for Q4 production of 310,000 to 320,000 BOE per day, a 3-5% sequential increase from Q3's 302,000 BOE per day average. For full year 2024, we expect 315,000 BOE per day, up 8% from 2023. Permian ramps to 182,000-188,000 BOE per day with Wolfcamp C infills and 12,500-foot laterals. Eagle Ford steady at 45,000-48,000 BOE per day. GoM to 48,000-52,000 BOE per day post-turnarounds. Key factors: rig efficiencies adding 25% more footage, ESP runtimes to 650 days, hedging 65% oil at $74 per barrel, and base decline management via workovers. Risks like hurricanes offset by insurance; upside from stronger IPs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Greg Sims with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Greg Sims: Could you please provide more color on capital expenditure breakdown and budget versus actual?

David Chen: Thanks, Greg. As detailed, H1 upstream Capex at $1.05 billion, 8% under budget. Drilling $365 million versus $390 million budgeted, thanks to Permian efficiencies at $1,450 per foot. Completions slightly over at $505 million versus $480 million due to proppant but offset by cube fracs. Facilities well under at $180 million versus $270 million with deferrals. Full-year holds at $2.1 billion midpoint, focused on high-IRR Permian.
